done_when: forge migrate keeps a file under an old-Forge folder when a tracked file outside the old-Forge folders references its path, and a test proves it

dismissals.because: src/forge/sync.py:271 .codex/skills/forge/SKILL.md is Forge's own generated adapter, not a client-owned file; migrate backs up its old content to .forge-migrate/kept/ before sync rewrites it, which is the intended handling, and this fix is about client files under old-Forge folders

findings.body: A tracked package.json referencing customized `.codex/skills/forge/SKILL.md` still loses access to that content after migration: this exclusion prevents preservation, so the customized file moves into `.forge-migrate/kept/`. Migration then calls `sync.write` at src/forge/migrate.py:746; src/forge/sync.py:271 supplies replacement content and :305 writes it at the original path. The package consequently reads different content despite its unchanged reference. The new command-level test explicitly expects this failure at tests/test_fix_forge_migrate_sets_aside_client_owned_fi.py:27–28. Preserve referenced client content through synchronization and change that test case to require the original content at its original path.

why: forge migrate sets aside client-owned files that live under old-Forge folders, such as myclaw's bundled factory/skills/gantry-admin/SKILL.md, even when the client's code or package still references them
